verdict.what: a fortified desert hall with a crenellated parapet and a central gate
verdict.style: Desert or Old West fortified civic/saloon hall, adobe-and-sandstone
verdict.looks: A long, low single-storey block seen from four sides. The walls are a terracotta or red-orange block with a tan sandstone-style trim: a plinth band at the base, a horizontal course line, and a thick cap band. Tan stone pilasters sit at the corners and the front. The top is a crenellated parapet, with alternating tan merlons and dark grey capstones. The front has a central recessed gate framed by stone piers, a stepped stone pedestal, a red carpet and small lanterns, flanked by two pale red-and-white awning strips over the wings. Window openings are cut into the red walls as tall slots with stone sills; some show tan or grey pillars inside. The side walls have a regular rhythm of three or four slot windows. The back is a plain red wall with a few window slots and a doorway-style recess.
verdict.summary: A clean, readable fort-hall with a good low massing and a nice gate, but the flat parapet reads as a lid on the box and the red walls are flat slabs with little depth, so it needs relief and roof work before it's placeable.
